arxiv.title: Chiral p-Wave Superconductivity Proximate to a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave in a Moiré Chern Band
arxiv.abstract: We study a spin-polarized moiré Chern band of twisted MoTe₂ with short-range repulsion, finding superconductivity proximate to a fractional Chern insulator at filling ν=2/3 and a topological charge density wave at ν=3/4. Exact diagonalization reveals pair binding over 0.7≲ν≲0.77, consistent with experiment, along with finite superfluid stiffness, chiral p-wave pairing correlations, and adiabatic connectivity to an attractive model. At weak repulsion, Kohn-Luttinger theory supports a Fermi-surface instability with the same pairing symmetry. The superconducting state has a Bogoliubov-de Gennes Chern number CBdG=-1, opposite to the normal-state Chern number at ν=1. Our results reveal interplay among superconductivity, fractional topology, and charge order.

arxiv.title: Topological Quantum Spin Liquids in a Ladder with Majorana fermions and p-wave Superconductivity
arxiv.abstract: In this article, we address the possibility of topological quantum spin liquids with only short-range (spin) correlations in the whole phase diagram in a ladder system, through an exactly solvable model which represents a generalization of the two-dimensional Kitaev honeycomb spin model to a ribbon geometry. This system gives rise to mathbbZ₂ gauge fields emerging in a static way in the ground state through Majorana fermions which then produce either 0 or π flux. Through a quantum field theory perspective, mathematical and Density Matrix Renormalization Group results, we present our progress on the geometrical, topological and physical classification of this model through observables navigating on the whole phase diagram presenting three spin-liquid phases with a spin gap and a metallic phase in the sense of Majorana fermions. We propose a bulk-edge correspondence revealing the presence of protected zero-energy Majorana fermions at the edge in the phases with a gap and revealing also the presence of itinerant Majorana fermions in the bulk in the topological liquid phase. The proposed approach allows us to distinguish between properties of the brickwall ladder giving rise to a special line and those of the square ladder allowing for the gapless Majorana liquid phase. This model gives some hope on finding solutions for topological quantum spin models, e.g. with π flux, on a squar

arxiv.title: Chiral superconductivity on a closed Klein bottle: a chirality wall and its Majorana seam spectrum
arxiv.abstract: We study a spinless π-flux lattice superconductor whose normal-state momentum-space fundamental domain is a Klein bottle. Within this model, a glide lift and a hidden antiunitary symmetry independently force the Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) Chern number to vanish. A diagonal pairing breaks the antiunitary obstruction exactly when its real part is nonzero; this is necessary, not sufficient, for a chiral phase. We derive explicit Pfaffians determining Chern parity and identify three analytic families of gap closings in a real-pairing section. For a chiral state on a closed real-space Klein bottle, the prescribed pairing and gluing produce a ΔC=2 chirality wall. A translation-invariant unfolding resolves two co-propagating Majorana branches. Their finite-size levels depend on circumference and holonomy; the near-zero pair is lifted at first order by allowed local seam perturbations. A cut-cylinder control has the same low-energy channel count, so gluing reconnects existing gapless content. We also distinguish literal gluing from deck projection: particle–hole symmetry exchanges the deck eigenblocks, precluding their interpretation as independent BdG quotient Hamiltonians. The contribution is a model-specific account of pairing compatibility and closed-surface seam spectra. arxiv.title: Coexistence of Superconductivity and Chern insulators with |C| ≥1 in twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene
arxiv.abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) has been demonstrated as a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated phases of matter. Here, we observe a coexistence of superconductivity and Chern insulators in a twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene moiré superlattice. Superconductivity, evidenced by a sharp transition with a critical temperature of ~180 mK, nonlinear I-V with a BKT temperature of 135 mK, and a signature of phase-sensitive interference patterns, emerges from a symmetry-breaking Fermi surface near v = -2 and D = 0, and it survives at a large in-plane magnetic field up to 2 T, strongly deviating from the Pauli limit. Moreover, we observe a strong modulation of the Ginzburg-Landau coherence length from 467 nm to 145 nm as the in-plane magnetic field increases from 0 to 2 T, whereas the critical current Ic barely changes. Unlike previous studies in RMG, we observe a competition between superconductivity and a correlated insulator at v = -2, monitored by displacement fields and twist angles. Note that we also observe integer Chern insulators with C = 1, 3, and -3 at v = 1/2, 1, and 3, respectively, for large D > 0 in the same superconducting device. The observations establish twisted rhombohedral graphene multilayers as a fascinating system to investigate unconventional superconductivity, high Chern number topology, and their interplay.

arxiv.title: Continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior in hybrid Josephson junction arrays
arxiv.abstract: We report finite-temperature scaling of voltage-driven quantum phase transitions in hybrid Josephson junction arrays. A dual-gate geometry separately tunes interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity, providing access to superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes. The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously with electrostatic tuning. Where the three regimes converge, the critical resistivity approaches h/4e², consistent with the self-dual limit, while the scaling exponent approaches the quantum-percolation estimate. Tuning toward stronger insulating behavior raises the critical resistivity and shifts the scaling exponent toward the classical-percolation value, while both parameters decrease toward the metallic regime. These results connect scaling regimes previously reported in different two-dimensional superconducting systems through continuous electrostatic control.

arxiv.title: Influence of pairing and correlations on transport properties in three-terminal superconducting nanostructure
arxiv.abstract: We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlation effects, inspecting their influence on the conductance and thermopower. Our calculations predict negative values of the nonlocal conductance and reversal of the Seebeck coefficient when the quantum dot ground state is represented by the BCS-type singlet configuration. These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.

arxiv.title: Evidence for an effective gauge field in flakes of superconducting 4Hb-TaS2
arxiv.abstract: Understanding the normal state of unconventional superconductors is central to uncovering the origin of superconductivity itself. Unconventional superconductivity often emerges from correlated electronic states characterized by intertwined symmetry-breaking orders. A striking example is 4Hb-TaS2, whose superconducting state exhibits a remarkable range of phenomena, including an unusual magnetic memory effect. Previous experiments showed that magnetic memory can be encoded above Tc and later revealed through spontaneous vortices below Tc, suggesting time-reversal symmetry breaking. However, since memory and vorticity are intertwined, this prevents establishing whether the effect results from trapped flux, weak conventional magnetism, or a true hidden electronic order. Here, we show that magnetic memory persists in the vortex-free Meissner regime of exfoliated 4Hb-TaS2 flakes, where it appears as a stable remanent modification of the superconducting screening response. Our results rule out explanations based on trapped vortices. Furthermore, the spatial profile of the flux generated by trained samples at zero field is inconsistent with conventional weak magnetism, suggesting a hidden electronic phase that imprints an effective flux on the superconducting condensate.

arxiv.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
arxiv.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a low-temperature anisotropic phase accompanied by a Fermi surface reconstruction. Near the stripe-to-superconductor transition, we also observed an additional thermodynamic phase transition from metallic stripes to pinned insulating stripes. The stripe-to-superconductor transition further exhibits an intriguing self-similarity that highlights the intimate relationship between the two orders. Our results pave the path for studying intertwined orders in moiré materials.

arxiv.title: Selective effects of selenium substitution on superconductivity and magnetic memory in 4Hb-TaS2
arxiv.abstract: Disorder plays a central role in correlated quantum materials, but its effects can be highly selective when several electronic orders coexist. The van der Waals heterostructure 4Hb-TaS2 provides such a case, combining superconductivity, charge-order tendencies, strong scattering, and magnetic memory manifested through spontaneous vortices. Here we use Se substitution as a controlled local perturbation of the disorder landscape in 4Hb-TaS2. We find that superconductivity remains remarkably robust while the magnetic memory is strongly suppressed at higher Se concentrations. These results show that Se substitution does not create the hidden magnetic memory, but instead selectively weakens its macroscopic manifestation. More broadly, they reveal a sharp separation between robust superconducting and hidden-memory phases, and a highly disorder-sensitive spontaneous-vortex response in 4Hb-TaS2.

arxiv.title: Majorana Zero Modes in Fractional Vortices
arxiv.abstract: Majorana zero modes (MZMs) are promising for topological quantum computation, with vortices in topological superconductors serving as a leading platform. Recent experiments show that integer Abrikosov vortices in iron-based superconductors can split into fractional vortices (FVs) carrying fractional flux quanta. We show that due to topological protection, MZMs hosted by FVs are spatially unfolded over the FV cores, while fermionic bound states remain localized at individual FV cores. This yields zero-bias conductance peaks in both local tunneling and nonlocal crossed Andreev reflection, offering an alternative MZM signature.

arxiv.title: Exceptional Superconducting Interfaces between Graphene and Atomic Chains in A15-MoRe
arxiv.abstract: Realizing highly transparent and magnetic-field-resilient superconducting contacts is a critical bottleneck for the advancement of two-dimensional (2D) quantum devices. Molybdenum-rhenium (MoRe) alloys have been empirically favored as they uniquely yield ballistic, highly transparent contacts to graphene that survive in high-magnetic-field regimes; however, the microscopic origin of this anomalous transparency has remained a long-standing puzzle. Here, we resolve this paradox by revealing that pristine graphene/MoRe interfaces are governed by the classical A15 superconducting phase. Combining low-temperature transport, X-ray diffraction, and atomic-resolution electron microscopy, we demonstrate that as-deposited MoRe spontaneously forms the A15 phase in direct contact with graphene, whereas thermal annealing triggers a phase transition to a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure that severely degrades the Josephson transparency. Crucially, the one-dimensional (1D) transition-metal atomic chains unique to the A15 structure exhibit a near-perfect lattice match (mismatch < 1%) with graphene edges. First-principles calculations further prove that the d-orbitals of these historically renowned 1D chains possibly hybridize with graphene's Dirac cone near the K point. arxiv.title: Thermalization-Controlled Superconducting Diode-Like Transport in Disordered Molybdenum and NbN Thin Films
arxiv.abstract: Superconducting diode effects are characterized by direction-dependent critical currents in the superconducting state. Here, we investigate diode-like transport in 128-nm-thick Mo thin film deposited on Si_SiO2 substrate by DC magnetron sputtering. The thin film exhibit a superconducting transition temperature TC of 5.8 K. Pronounced current-direction asymmetry and hysteresis are observed in current-voltage characteristics measured in a closed-cycle refrigerator. In contrast, the same thin film exhibits a substantially more symmetric response in a 14T cryogenic system with improved sample thermalization. We attribute this strong dependence on the measurement environment to electrothermal effects arising from current-induced Joule heating and finite thermal relaxation. As the current approaches the superconducting-to-resistive switching condition, the emergence of a resistive component leads to a rapid increase in Joule heating, raising the sample temperature and modifying the switching condition. Conversely, during the resistive-to-superconducting transition, residual heating and finite thermal relaxation reduce the switching current. Since P is equal to I2R it is independent of current polarity, the observed asymmetry is not associated with polarity-dependent Joule heating but with the interplay of thermal relaxation, sweep history, and thermal boundary conditions. arxiv.title: Position- and Temperature-Dependent Responsivity in a KID-Based Phonon-Mediated Detector
arxiv.abstract: We report on the position- and temperature-dependent response of a kinetic inductance phonon-mediated (KIPM) detector. To study position-dependence, we used a controllable mirror attached to a micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) to steer optical light with a 100 μm spot size over the backside of the cryogenic detector. With both pulsed and continuous operation of the LED, we observe features of the detector housing and find that the signal is strongest when the LED is pointed directly at the KID. The "off-KID" response is measured to be 34% of the "on-KID" response and is largely independent of direction. We model phonon propagation and collection in the KIPM detector with G4CMP and assert that the isotropic angular dependence is unlikely to be due to discrete phonon absorption "sinks", such as the microwave feedline or the device mounting points, but can be explained instead by an isotropic energy loss in the crystal. We furthermore utilize the temperature flexibility of the MEMS and KIPM detector system to investigate temperature-dependent responsivity, both at the sensor level (i.e., frequency shifts in the KID) and at the detector level (i.e., position dependence). We fit the KID's response to a two-component heat capacity and present the model as an alternative way to understand the KID's response to absorbed energy. arxiv.title: Local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a two-orbital s± superconductor
arxiv.abstract: We study the local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a self-consistent two-orbital s± superconductor. For a local s-wave tip that couples equally to the two orbitals, anomalous spectral contributions of opposite sign nearly cancel in the clean sample. Nonmagnetic impurities redistribute these contributions and can reverse the local coupling without a corresponding π phase shift of the bond pair fields. Negative coupling appears at off-center sites at weaker impurity potentials than at the impurity site. The impurity-induced change is concentrated at lower quasiparticle energies, while states over a broader energy range contribute to the total clean and impurity couplings. In zero field, the coupling also changes sign as the tip gap is varied, and increasing the tunneling strength can reverse the m=1 sine component of the current without changing the sample state. At the chosen coherence-peak energy, increasing impurity strength mainly changes the relative intensities of existing quasiparticle-interference features. In a self-consistent two-vortex state, the Josephson response develops a spatially varying phase relative to the condensate. arxiv.title: Coexistence of superconductivity and magnetic order in BaFe₂S₃: evidence for orbital-selective delocalization
arxiv.abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. The quasi-one-dimensional spin-ladder compound \bfs\ serves as a unique platform to study this interplay, as it lacks the two-dimensional square lattice characteristic of most iron-based superconductors. Here, we combine high-pressure x-ray and neutron diffraction, x-ray emission spectroscopy, and electrical transport to map its structural, magnetic, and electronic evolution into the superconducting regime. We \revised{observe} a striking pressure-induced decoupling: while the long-range stripe-type antiferromagnetic order remains remarkably robust under pressure up to the onset of superconductivity, the local iron magnetic moment is suppressed by nearly 80%. This dichotomy \revised{points to an orbital-selective mechanism}, where specific Fe 3d electrons remain localized to sustain magnetism while others delocalize to form the itinerant and superconducting state. \revised{Superconductivity emerges while long-range magnetic order is still present, revealing that the two coexist in \bfs, which we attribute to} the selective response of multiorbital electronic degrees of freedom.

arxiv.title: A First-Order Phase Transition in Spin-Imbalanced BCS Theory of Superconductivity
arxiv.abstract: We study a translation-invariant BCS functional of superconductivity for a system of spin-1/2 fermions with spin-dependent chemical potentials, μ₊neqμ₋. Numerical work of Caldas and Mota and analytical work of Freiji, Hainzl, and Seiringer has suggested an unusual first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS models, in which the normal state becomes globally unstable while remaining locally stable. Here, we prove that a first-order phase transition occurs in such spin-imbalanced BCS functionals. For each sufficiently small fixed spin imbalance and sufficiently low temperature, there is a coexistence coupling λfo strictly below the linear-stability threshold λlin of the normal state at which the Cooper pair density exhibits a nonzero jump and the minimized energy has a kink. The methodological insight is a coercivity estimate obtained by decomposing the BCS energy minimization into two parts, where the “inner” problem minimizes over the one-particle density matrices at fixed pairing and can be exactly solved by a Legendre–Fenchel transform.

arxiv.title: Separating the Density Wave Phase from Zero-Resistance Superconductivity in La₄Ni₃O₁₀
arxiv.abstract: Identifying the key ingredients for superconductivity under pressure in the Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates remains a formidable challenge, due to a complex interplay between structural variations, oxygen content and location, electronically ordered phases, and the need for high pressures to reach the superconducting phase. To disentangle these complex inter-dependencies, here we study a series of clean single crystals of trilayer La₄Ni₃O₁₀. We discover that enhanced biaxial, compressive pressures induce a zero-resistance state at a 60% lower pressure compared to previous reports. At the same time, we completely separate the low-pressure density wave phase from superconductivity, effectively ruling out that soft, quantum critical fluctuations of the density wave order parameter act as the pairing glue in this system. Our results establish biaxial, in-plane pressures as a powerful tool for promoting superconductivity in nickelates, unifying the required pressure scales for superconductivity in different Ruddlesden-Popper structures, and providing a connection to the recently discovered thin film samples.

arxiv.title: Quantum Gate Engineering in Superconducting NISQ Platforms: Experimental Methods and Emerging Directions
arxiv.abstract: This review aims to provide researchers, experimentalists, and quantum engineers with an updated and technically grounded perspective on the implementation of quantum gates in superconducting NISQ devices. The goal is to establish a comprehensive bridge between theoretical quantum circuit synthesis and its practical, experimental implementation, focusing on superconducting quantum technologies. We systematically examine the diverse landscape of superconducting qubits and processor architectures, ranging from conventional transmons to alternative and unconventional designs, evaluating their unique design trade-offs, connectivity constraints, device physics, and materials impact. Moving from theory to actual implementation, we detail how single- and two-qubit operations are synthesized via microwave-driven and flux-activated pulses. We here present our pulse engineering, wave shaping, calibration workflows, demonstrating how to bridge the gap between abstract gate models and real-world hardware limitations in the direction of a hardware-software co-design framework. To validate these operations, we choose benchmarking methodologies with the purpose to get the more efficient metric for the specific evaluation aspect, including truth tables and quantum process tomography. arxiv.title: Coherent Electronic Lensing in Proximitized Graphene
arxiv.abstract: Spatially resolved control of coherent electron transport offers a route to understanding and engineering interference phenomena in hybrid superconducting devices. Here, we use Scanning Gate Microscopy (SGM) to investigate Fabry-Pérot (FP) interference in the n-p-n cavity of a ballistic graphene Josephson junction. Spatial maps of the superconducting switching current and normal-state conductance reveal circular interference fringes arising from two distinct effects of the SGM tip potential. A global shift of the Fermi wave vector modulates the FP resonances of the cavity, while a local perturbation produces additional oscillations that persist at fixed Fermi wave vector as the tip bias is varied. An analytical model identifies the origin of this local response with coherent electron lensing, in which the tip modifies the phase accumulated along interfering trajectories. The measured fringe patterns in the switching current indicate that this mechanism affects superconducting transport, consistent with tip-induced shifts of the resonance conditions for Andreev bound states. These results establish SGM as a tunable local lens for controlling interference in superconducting ballistic graphene devices.

arxiv.title: Layer-Parity Control of the Superconducting Diode Effect in Monolayer NbSe₂
arxiv.abstract: The superconducting diode effect is often associated with finite-momentum pairing, although model studies indicate that rectification reflects the asymmetry of the free energy about its minimum rather than the equilibrium pair momentum itself. Using a Wannier-based, self-consistent finite-mathbfQ Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach with a Fermi-surface-adaptive quadrature that converges the critical currents, we show that the layer parity and orientation of magnetic proximity select the diode response of monolayer NbSe₂. For in-plane exchange, the equilibrium pair momentum mathbfQrmeq and the diode efficiency are both linear in the layer-odd exchange contrast: parallel proximity on the two Se sublayers is reciprocal, and antiparallel proximity doubles the response. An out-of-plane component separates the two observables. It leaves mathbfQrmeq nearly unchanged but, through pair breaking, suppresses the efficiency by more than an order of magnitude and, at low temperature, reverses it. Purely out-of-plane exchange, for which C₃ symmetry forbids a helical term, keeps mathbfQrmeq=0 yet produces a trigonal diode effect, controlled by the layer-even exchange and larger than the in-plane one above 0.65~meV at low temperature. arxiv.title: Direct real-space imaging of sign-reversal superconducting state by scanning Josephson tunneling
arxiv.abstract: Phase-sensitive experiments based on Josephson tunneling have been considered as a pivotal method to determine the pairing symmetry in high-temperature (high-Tc) cuprate superconductors. However, in iron-based superconductors, traditional phase-sensitive experiments face setbacks because of the complexity of pairing symmetry in multiband systems. Here, using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), we report the half-unit-cell periodic Josephson tunneling modulations in monolayer high-Tc Fe(Te,Se) film epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001). The Josephson tunneling almost vanishes along the lines connecting next-nearest-neighbor Fe atoms under an s-wave superconducting tip. Combined with single-particle tunneling spectra showing the full superconducting gap, our experimental results are consistent with the sign-reversal nodeless d-wave pairing symmetry. Our findings provide sub-unit-cell scale superconducting phase information for understanding the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity. We anticipate our work as a starting point for atomically resolved Josephson interference experiments using SJTM in various unconventional superconductors.

arxiv.title: Influences of N₂ flow rate on the superconducting properties and dimensionality of epitaxial TiN thin films
arxiv.abstract: TiN thin films have received great attention in the field of superconducting quantum computing due to their low loss characteristics derived from stable chemical and thermal properties, as well as excellent electrical conductivity. In this study, TiN thin films with a thickness of 35 nm were epitaxially grown on MgO substrates using the DC reactive magnetron sputtering technique. The crystal structure, film thickness, and surface morphology of the thin films were characterized. The films exhibit a very flat surface with a root mean square roughness of only a few tenths of a nanometer. The influences of nitrogen (N₂) flow rate on the surface morphology, superconducting transition temperature (Tc), residual resistivity ratio (RRR), normal-state resistivity (ρn), upper critical field, and superconducting dimensionality were investigated systematically. The experimental results show that the TiN film deposited with a N₂ flow rate of 1.5 sccm exhibits optimal performance, including the highest Tc (4.93 K), the largest RRR, the lowest ρn, and the lowest slope of the out-of-film upper critical field near Tc. Moreover, it is found that the background vacuum inside the growth chamber has a significant impact on the superconducting properties of TiN films, and the degradation of vacuum degree can lead to the decrease of Tc. arxiv.title: Parity-Resolved Many-Body Kinetics of a Topological Qubit under Nonequilibrium Phonon Pulses
arxiv.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two 2,μm proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn–Oreg model, microscopic electron–phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75–1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. Factorized Boltzmann kinetics neglects quasiparticle correlations and overestimates residual parity flips. At equal deposited energy density, phonon spectra yield different excitation probabilities and coherence losses. arxiv.title: Field theory of competing phases in the interacting Kitaev chain
arxiv.abstract: We study the interacting Kitaev chain with nearest-neighbor interactions and finite chemical potential using a combination of bosonization and density-matrix renormalization-group calculations. Focusing away from special exactly solvable lattice limits, we develop a continuum field-theoretic description of the generic finite-density interacting regime, where doping nonperturbatively modifies the competition between superconducting pairing and commensurate charge ordering. We show that the phase diagram consists of an intermediate incommensurate Luttinger liquid between the topological superconducting and commensurate charge-density-wave Mott phases, as well as a trivial band-insulating regime at large chemical potential. The commensurate–incommensurate and incommensurate–topological-superconducting phase boundaries are governed by Pokrovsky–Talapov and Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless criticality, respectively. We analyze the interacting topological superconducting regime and its boundary excitations. At the semiclassical level, and explicitly in the free-fermion boundary theory, the topological phase supports exponentially localized Majorana edge modes at interfaces between topological and trivial regions. arxiv.title: A B₁g phonon unlocks d-wave superconductivity in the repulsive Hubbard model
arxiv.abstract: Using numerically exact finite-temperature quantum Monte Carlo, we demonstrate that a B₁g phonon coupled to the doped t-t' repulsive Hubbard model produces genuine d-wave superconductivity at a substantial transition temperature, in excess of either interaction alone. The observed trends suggest that stronger Hubbard repulsion may cooperate with the phonon to further raise the pairing scale. The enhancement persists at stronger repulsion within the accessible window, limited by the fermion sign problem, and follows a common trend across phonon frequencies Ω when organized by a retardation scale 2πT/Ω. We also find a well-defined superconducting dome in doping, echoing a characteristic feature of correlated superconductors. Our results identify the B₁g phonon as a plausible microscopic ingredient for robust d-wave superconductivity in the Hubbard model and suggest a concrete, physically motivated route toward materials with higher superconducting transition temperatures.

arxiv.title: Approaching Landauer's limit in a single superconducting vortex memory bit
arxiv.abstract: This work investigates the energy required to manipulate a memory bit using a superconducting vortex confined in a nanoscale double-well pinning potential. In the experiments, various double-well systems subjected to sinusoidal forces is explored, and the effects of both driving force and frequency is analyzed. Results reveal characteristic stochastic resonance behavior for weak drives and adiabatic manipulation at strong, low-frequency drives. Although our experimental method requires a steady sinusoidal drive incompatible with Landauer's erasure protocol, our numerical analysis demonstrates that the work required for such bit manipulation (erasure) is within an order of magnitude of Landauer's limit (kB T ln2) at 4.2 K. These findings open possibilities for creating highly efficient memory elements that could be integrated with cryogenic quantum circuits or function as topological quantum computing qubits; thereby contributing to memory devices with lower energy consumption and mitigating the escalating global energy demand in the computing industry.

arxiv.title: Superconductivity and local stacking polymorphism in LaNiGa2 thin films
arxiv.abstract: LaNiGa2 has attracted considerable interest as a candidate unconventional superconductor, particularly due to its reported time-reversal symmetry breaking and nonsymmorphic crystal structure hosting symmetry-protected electronic band degeneracies. Here, we report the growth and characterization of superconducting LaNiGa2 thin films on MgO substrates by magnetron sputtering. X-ray diffraction reveals highly crystalline, (010)-oriented films with well-defined in-plane alignment and rotational twinning. Electrical transport measurements establish superconductivity with a transition temperature of approximately 1 K. Atomic-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals local variations in crystallographic orientation and interlayer stacking, with a predominantly Cmcm structure containing minority Cmmm regions. The coexistence of these closely related structures reveals local stacking polymorphism that is difficult to distinguish using conventional X-ray diffraction. These findings establish a superconducting LaNiGa2 thin-film platform and provide new insight into the local crystal structure of a material whose electronic properties and superconducting pairing remain under active investigation.

arxiv.title: Point-contact spectroscopy of electron-phonon interactions and anisotropy of superconducting energy gaps in 2H-NbSe₂
arxiv.abstract: The superconducting state of 2H-NbSe₂ was studied using point contacts for two main orientations of the contact axis relative to the principal crystallographic orientations: along the c-axis and in the ab plane. For contacts oriented in the ab plane, dependencies proportional to the electron-phonon interaction function were obtained, which agree perfectly with the theoretical calculation. It was found that the features on the experimental curves associated with the electron-phonon interaction extend to energies twice the cutoff energy of the phonon spectrum and have an amplitude of the same order of magnitude throughout the entire energy range. It has been theoretically demonstrated that the features at energies exceeding the boundaries of the phonon density of states are caused by two-phonon scattering processes of non-equilibrium phonons on Andreev electrons. A criterion for the undisturbed nature of the crystal lattice in the region where gap features form has been found. Using 2H-NbSe₂-Cu heterocontacts in the superconducting state, a study of energy gaps was conducted for two orientations of the NbSe₂ crystal: along the c-axis and in the ab plane. It was found that the superconducting energy gaps are anisotropic; specifically, three gaps were identified in the ab plane, whereas only two were observed in the c direction.

arxiv.title: Structural supermodulation enables resonant Raman determination of crystalline orientation in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x flakes
arxiv.abstract: Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (Bi-2212) is a d-wave superconductor with unconventional properties intrinsic to the material itself. These properties are of growing interest for quantum technologies in electronics and photonics, and twisted Josephson junctions can make direct use of them. However, Bi-2212 is strongly anisotropic, and it is challenging to find its crystal axes in flakes in advance, which limits device engineering. Here, we show that polarized resonant Raman spectroscopy reveals the orientation of both the a and b axes of Bi-2212 optically and non-destructively. By correlating Laue diffraction, HAADF-STEM and polarized Raman scattering on the same bulk crystal, we assign the b axis, along which the incommensurate structural supermodulation propagates, to the intensity maximum of the 27 cm-1 supermodulation mode, which varies in counter-phase with the 118 cm-1 Bi/Sr mode, along the a axis. Multi-wavelength measurements (458, 532, 660 nm) show that resulting in-plane contrast peaks at 532 nm and nearly vanishes at 660 nm, indicating that the anisotropy originates from an electronic resonance induced by the supermodulation. Using this resonance, we determine the crystallographic axes of exfoliated flakes and access their symmetry channels, providing a rapid orientation tool for cuprate van der Waals heterostructures.

arxiv.title: Magnetic Imaging with High Spatial Resolution Using a Single Niobium-Nitride-Based Three-Dimensional Nanobridge Junction
arxiv.abstract: The nanobridge junctions (NBJs) allow the miniaturization of the Superconducting Quantum Interference Device (SQUID) and improve the spatial resolution of scanning SQUID microscopy. However, the SQUID loop diameter imposed a fundamental limit on the resolution. In this work, we proposed a single niobium-nitride-based three-dimensional nanobridge junction (NbN-3D-NBJ) alternative to the nanoSQUID for high-resolution magnetic imaging. The critical current of an NbN-3D-NBJ showed an nearly monotonic dependence on the external magnetic field, enabling nanoscale mapping of the magnetic field distribution by measuring the junction's critical current with an intrinsic noise level of 100 nT/Hz^1/2. Using a NbN-3D-NBJ probe, we successfully imaged an Abrikosov vortex in a niobium film with a minimal full width at half maxima (FWHM) of 530 nm, constrained by the distance from the junction to the probe tip edge. Furthermore, we resolved 80 nm spacings between the superconducting nanowires utilizing a second probe with an optimized junction-to-tip distance. Thus, the single 3D NbN NBJ probe has been demonstrated as an effective approach for magnetic imaging with ultra-high spatial resolution.

arxiv.title: Nano-Nb Superconducting 3D Josephson Junctions Arrays in Cu-Normal Matrix: Superconducting Phase Coherence and Quantum Fluctuations Properties
arxiv.abstract: To address the complex interplay of microstructural evolution, phase separation, superconductivity coherence and quantum fluctuations, we prepared Cuxwt%Nb series of granular samples by rapidly cooling, where the niobium concentration varied (x = 3, 5, 15, 20). By employing this method, we successfully obtained samples characterized by well-defined precipitates of niobium, featuring regular sizes and grain spacing. The goal was to establish a systematic and robust method approach for obtaining samples with different of sub-micrometric precipitates distributions but also to investigate their superconducting properties. Structural characterization by optical and Scanning Electron Microscopy, dc Mdc[H,T] ac inductive , as well the magneto-transport measures rhodc[H,T], Rdc[V,I.H,T], I[V,H,T] and [H,T,I] were done. Also, using a micro Hall sensor with 10 measuring transverse voltage bridges regularly distributed, we were able to obtain the real external applied magnetic field value inside of the chamber sample space. Thus e studied the dependence of configuration of the Nb grains in the superconducting coupling order parameter properties that connects the grains superconductors to the normal Cu matrix. We verify through magnetization and transport measures the signature of the double transition. This, when we apply current of different intensities, in the transport measures, and di

arxiv.title: A pathway to improve Nb₃Sn for SRF accelerator cavities via Zr inclusion
arxiv.abstract: Nb₃Sn has the potential to exceed the performance of niobium-based superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) cavities, both in particle accelerators and in high-Q₀ cavities operating in multi-tesla magnetic fields for axion dark matter searches. We studied how the incorporation of Zr into the Nb₃Sn matrix by co-sputtering affects the microstructure and superconducting properties of Nb₃Sn films. As the atomic fraction of Zr increased, the surface morphology improved and the bulk and surface void densities decreased. At the optimal Zr content, the superconducting properties improved and a thinner surface niobium oxide formed. These results identify co-sputtered Nb₃Sn:Zr as a promising material to advance the performance limits of SRF cavities.

arxiv.title: Vortex anisotropy in chiral and nematic superconductors with strain
arxiv.abstract: Unconventional superconductors with a two-component order parameter support the existence of a rotational symmetry breaking nematic phase and a time-reversal symmetry breaking chiral phase. A recent experiment on 4Hb-TaS₂ surprisingly shows both twofold anisotropy in Hc₂, which suggests nematic superconductivity, as well as isotropic vortices at low temperatures, which suggest chiral superconductivity. To resolve this apparent conundrum we write down the appropriate Ginzburg-Landau equations and develop a numerically efficient algorithm for finding vortex solutions, allowing us to study their shape and anisotropy over a broad parameter range. We also demonstrate analytically that, to leading order, the vortex anisotropy is independent of strain in the nematic case, but is linearly dependent on it in the chiral phase, providing a possible way to distinguish the two phases. Using all these results we show that, in the presence of strain, in a large parameter regime the system behaves nematically near the transition, leading to an anisotropy of Hc₂, but is dominantly chiral away from the transition, leading to parametrically smaller vortex anisotropy, in line with the experiment.

arxiv.title: Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
arxiv.abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking – how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe₂, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenologic

arxiv.title: Determination of the Magnetic Penetration Depth from Finite-Element Susceptibility Calculations of Spheroidal and Cylindrical Superconductors
arxiv.abstract: The magnetic penetration depth, λ, is a fundamental parameter of the superconducting state and is commonly determined from precision measurements of the magnetic susceptibility, χ, in the Meissner state. However, extracting λ from such measurements requires an accurate treatment of geometry-dependent demagnetization effects, for which analytic results are only available in a limited number of cases. Here we present a finite-element analysis of the magnetic response of three dimensional superconducting spheroids and cylinders with finite penetration depth. By calculating the magnetic moment and susceptibility, χ(λ), over a wide range of aspect ratios, we quantify the shape-dependent Meissner response and extract effective demagnetization factors in the λ→0 limit. For small but finite λ, we further determine effective sample dimensions from the initial variation of χ(λ) and propose an improved analytical expression for these. Our results provide a high-precision procedure for determining λ from volume-exclusion based susceptibility measurements and should be directly applicable to the characterization of novel superconducting materials.

arxiv.title: Proximity-Induced Giant Majorana Spin Response in a UTe₂-Metal Film Heterostructure
arxiv.abstract: We establish an experimentally accessible route to identifying Majorana surface states through their intrinsic Ising spin response, using UTe₂ as a concrete platform. The key is to extend the Majorana correlations into an adjacent metallic film via the superconducting proximity effect, thereby making the otherwise surface-localized response accessible to NMR measurements. Remarkably, disorder further sharpens the Majorana signature: impurity scattering suppresses the conventional p-wave proximity correlations while preserving the Majorana contribution, yielding a giant Ising-anisotropic enhancement of the NMR relaxation rate. This approach also offers a powerful means to distinguish among candidate pairing symmetries.

arxiv.title: The fate of s± superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La₃Ni₂O₇
arxiv.abstract: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La₃Ni₂O₇ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an s± superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like d-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full SU(2) particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual U(1) treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La₃Ni₂O₇, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of s± symmetry in favor of d-wave pairing.

arxiv.title: Growth Phase Map of α and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
arxiv.abstract: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of α-Ta(110), α-Ta(111), and metastable β-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al₂O₃(0001) at 300-900 °C while varying the O₂ partial pressure from a 5.5×10⁻¹¹ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to 2.23×10⁻⁴ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio (2ΦO_₂/ΦTa≤4.8×10⁻⁶ to 19). Without added oxygen, α-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O₂ pressure of only 2.5×10⁻⁹ Torr (2ΦO_₂/ΦTa=2.2×10⁻⁴), α-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 °C, decreasing to 65% at 900 °C. Substantial β-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 °C and disappearing at 900 °C. The apparent β(001)/α(110) selection energy of 1.07±0.16 eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.

arxiv.title: Local Broadband Gigahertz Spectroscopy via SQUID-on-Tip DC Readout
arxiv.abstract: Superconducting microwave circuits are shaped by their local electromagnetic environment, yet standard microwave measurements do not resolve the local fields and device features that govern their behavior. Here, we combine microwave spectroscopy, nanoscale magnetic sensing, and topographic imaging in a single tapping-mode SQUID-on-tip microscope. The nonlinear Josephson response converts local GHz excitations into Shapiro steps, enabling quantitative measurements of microwave frequency signals and their excitation strength using only DC readout. Applied to a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator, local spectroscopy reproduces the power-dependent resonance and nonlinear bifurcation observed in microwave transmission measurements. Spatially resolved measurements map the microwave response while simultaneously recording topography and static magnetic features, including vortices and Meissner screening currents. Electromagnetic simulations reveal how coupling through the superconducting probe leads limits spatial resolution and guides localized detector designs. Together, these capabilities establish a platform for correlating microwave circuit dynamics with the local structural and magnetic environment of superconducting devices.

arxiv.title: Momentum-resolved thermodynamics and barrier-free order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors under a Zeeman field
arxiv.abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can enhance the critical Zeeman field of clean superconductors beyond the Pauli limit. We develop a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy to investigate spin-singlet s-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric SOC. The SOC component perpendicular to the Zeeman field enhances the critical field and suppresses first-order features, whereas the parallel component favors Pauli-limited thermodynamic behavior. Applying this framework to Rashba superconductors and Ising superconductors with weak Rashba SOC, we identify the origin of the abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter at the critical field. Competing angular contributions produce a nearly flat free-energy landscape, allowing a barrier-free order-parameter collapse distinct from the conventional Pauli-limited first-order transition.

arxiv.title: Higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation by a superconducting antenna with vortices
arxiv.abstract: The interaction between superconductivity and magnetism provides new routes for controlling nonlinear excitations in hybrid systems. While dc-driven Abrikosov vortices (fluxons) are known to interact with spin waves, the ability of confined, nearly harmonic vortex oscillations to generate higher-frequency spin-wave modes remains unexplored. Here, by combining time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau modeling with spectral analysis of the microwave near field, we demonstrate higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation driven by a superconducting microstrip antenna in the Shubnikov phase. Unlike conventional harmonic-generation mechanisms associated with nonlinear magnetization dynamics, the magnetic layer remains a linear receiver, whereas the superconducting antenna generates the nonlinear microwave field. We show that nearly sinusoidal vortex motion and the accompanying redistribution of superconducting screening currents produce higher harmonics that couple to spin-wave modes. This response arises from spatial-to-temporal transduction, whereby harmonic vortex motion and the associated redistribution of screening currents convert a spatially nonuniform magnetic-field profile into higher temporal harmonics. Magnetic flux quanta thus act as active nonlinear elements for frequency conversion, extending the accessible spin-wave frequency range in superconducting–magnonic hybrids.

arxiv.title: Magnetic susceptibility and superfluid density of inhomogeneous superconducting films: the Tc-mosaic model
arxiv.abstract: Whole-sample and mutual-inductance part-sample measurements of the linear magnetic susceptibility, χ, of superconducting films are routinely used to obtain the London penetration depth, λ(T), assuming uniform superconductivity. However, spatially resolved probes show that many films of current interest are inhomogeneous on micrometer scales. Here we ask whether a distribution of local transition temperatures in a fully gapped film can produce an apparent line-nodal, T-linear λ(T). The film is modeled as a random Voronoi mosaic of domains with Tc distributed between Tc,min and Tc,maₓ with s-wave (also d-wave, for comparison) London response inside each domain. We show that detectable screening appears only below the percolation temperature, Tp, and the transition broadens with the spread of Tc. For s-wave domains, λ(T) remains activated for any Tc,min>0. Only for Tc,min=0 does it become a power law, Δλ∝Tⁿ with n≈1.7, but then the onset of screening drops to Tp=Tc,maₓ/2. Weighting the Tc distribution towards Tc→0 (more low-Tc domains) can bring n closer to 1 (n≈1.2), but simultaneously pushes the apparent transition, Tp, more than an order of magnitude below Tc,maₓ. For d-wave domains, the linear term survives, and its relative slope is enhanced almost fourfold for Tc,min=0.
