arxiv.title: Nodeless d-wave pairing in monolayer FeSe revealed by intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry
arxiv.abstract: The Josephson effect provides a direct phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order and has played a central role in identifying unconventional pairing symmetries1-6. Conventional Josephson interferometry, however, extracts phase information through engineered junction geometries and crystallographic orientations, rather than by resolving the internal phase structure of the pair state within a single unit cell. Here, we use a superconducting Nb tip to realize atomic-scale Josephson interferometry in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3. Despite a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum, the local Josephson response exhibits a striking intra-unit-cell pattern, with maxima centred on Fe-Fe bonds and robust nodal lines along the Fe-Se directions. We show that these nodal lines arise from destructive interference between Josephson tunnelling amplitudes associated with opposite-sign pairing components. Microscopic calculations reproduce the observed spatial pattern and identify it as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing. Our results establish intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry as a local phase-sensitive probe of pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors.

arxiv.title: Fermionic superfluid transition and pairing scale separation in the kagome flat band
arxiv.abstract: Flat-band systems provide a promising platform for exploring exotic correlated phases owing to quenched kinetic energy and enhanced interaction effects. In this work, we investigate the flat-band superfluid transition in the attractive kagome Hubbard model using large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations accelerated by fast Fourier transforms and delay updates. Through systematic calculations of the transition temperature, spin susceptibility, and density compressibility, we establish the finite-temperature phase diagram at the flat-band filling ρ=5/3 and find a clear linear scaling of the superfluid transition temperature with the interaction strength, Tc=0.0314|U|. Our results reveal a wide separation of temperature scales between local pair formation and global phase coherence, which stabilizes a broad intermediate supercompressible bosonic fluid region of preformed pairs that bridges the normal Fermi gas and the flat-band superfluid. We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-materia

arxiv.title: Phase fluctuations dominated superconductivity in a thick Granular Boron-Doped Diamond film
arxiv.abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of a 1.2-μm-thick granular boron-doped diamond film, where tightly packed grains form a disordered network of Josephson junctions. The film exhibits a sharp superconducting transition at a critical temperature, T_c ~ 3 K. Its transport properties are well described by the Ambegaokar-Halperin theory of phase fluctuations. Direct measurements of the penetration depth using a two-coil mutual inductance technique reveal classic phase-fluctuation-dominated behavior: below T_c, the superfluid density (n_s) varies linearly over a wide temperature range - a hallmark of thermal phase fluctuations - before crossing over to a T^2 dependence at ultra-low temperatures. Both the large low-temperature penetration depth, λ(0) ~ 8.8 μm, and the slope of the linear ns variation in the thermal regime reveal a remarkably low superfluid stiffness in the range of 0.5-0.8 K. These results establish granular boron-doped diamond films as an excellent model system for investigating the role of long-wavelength phase fluctuations in three-dimensional superconductors.

arxiv.title: Universal Scaling of the Little-Parks Oscillation Amplitude
arxiv.abstract: The Little-Parks effect played a pivotal role in establishing fluxoid quantization in doubly connected superconductors and providing early evidence for electron pairing, central to BCS theory. More recently, it has emerged as an important phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order. Yet the amplitude of the Little-Parks oscillation has never been fully understood theoretically, as the conventional mean-field Ginzburg-Landau description does not account for its pronounced temperature dependence. Here, we develop a universal theoretical framework incorporating thermal fluctuations in reduced-dimensional superconducting rings. By analyzing Little-Parks measurements across multiple superconductors, we show that the resulting scaling quantitatively captures the temperature-dependent oscillation amplitudes over a broad range of materials and device geometries, resolving the long-standing discrepancy between theory and experiment.

arxiv.title: Tilt-Controlled Multi-Gap Superconductivity in Type-II Weyl Semimetals
arxiv.abstract: In type-II Weyl semimetals, strongly tilted Weyl cones produce coexisting electron and hole pockets, a natural multi-band setting for superconductivity, yet how the tilt controls the number and relative size of the superconducting gaps remains unclear. Here we classify the symmetry-allowed on-site pairing channels of a simple time-reversal symmetric tilted Weyl-semimetal model with D₄ symmetry and identify the fully symmetric A₁ channel as the leading instability for attractive on-site interactions, supporting a fully gapped two-gap state. The tilt acts as a microscopic control parameter, redistributing the band-resolved pairing susceptibility between the two Fermi-surface sectors rather than simply rescaling the total density of states. Once the tilt sufficiently enhances the secondary channel, a robust secondary gap develops and can exceed the primary gap even at weaker effective coupling, while inter-gap coupling locks both gaps to a common critical superconducting temperature. The Weyl cone tilt thus controls the emergence and hierarchy of multi-gap superconductivity.

arxiv.title: Field misalignment effect on the in-plane magnetoresistance in the high-temperature superconductor FeSe/SrTiO3
arxiv.abstract: The azimuthal angular dependence of the in-plane magnetoresistance provides a powerful probe for detecting rotational symmetry breaking in superconductors, which has significant implications for understanding the superconducting pairing symmetry and the intertwined orders. However, in two-dimensional or layered superconductors with strong anisotropy between in-plane and out-of-plane critical fields, measuring the in-plane magnetoresistance is particularly challenging as it is extremely sensitive to the field misalignment. Here we perform systematic electrical transport measurements on ultrathin FeSe films grown on SrTiO3 substrates. By remounting the same FeSe film to change the field misalignment, two qualitatively different angular dependences of the in-plane magnetoresistance are observed in the superconducting transition region, indicating the extreme sensitivity of the measurement to field misalignment. The observed anisotropic in-plane magnetoresistance can be well captured by our geometric model considering the field misalignment effect. Our work provides a practical framework for disentangling the misalignment effect and investigating the in-plane rotational symmetry breaking in two-dimensional or layered superconductors.

arxiv.title: Scattering and Schmid-Bulgadaev Transition in Qubits Based on Josephson Junction Chains
arxiv.abstract: A Josephson junction subject to an ohmic dissipative environment undergoes a zero-temperature quantum phase transition called Schmid-Bulgadaev transition form an insulating state to a superconducting state upon increasing the impedance of the environment above the resistance quantum. Superconducting qubits based on Josephson junction chains represent a system where it is possible to dynamically explore both sides of this transition by probing the scattering of individual plasma modes of the junction chain on a SQUID at the boundary which was achieved in recent experiments. Here, we provide a theoretical analysis of the scattering in the system paying special attention to the non-perturbative superconducting regime. We find that in this regime, a specific diagrammatic resummation must be performed in order to correctly account for fluctuation renormalization of the SQUID's potential. We find analytic expressions for the modes' frequency shifts and quality factors which together provide a full description of scattering. We argue that the non-perturbative nature of the superconducting phase manifests itself through a power-law dependence of the frequency shifts on the SQUID flux and through non-monotonous dependence of the quality factors on the mode frequency. Our predictions may be readily verified in modern low-temperature experiments.

arxiv.title: Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
arxiv.abstract: Can the correlations favoring electron crystallization also generate superconductivity in the neighboring metal? We investigate this possibility in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with repulsive Coulomb interactions. Self-consistent Hartree–Fock calculations identify a commensurate triangular Wigner-crystal state. To investigate pairing on the metallic side, we construct a crossing-symmetric particle–hole vertex using coupled parquet and Bethe–Salpeter equations, incorporating exchange vertex corrections beyond polarization-bubble screening. Near crystallization, the enhanced electronic correlations generate an effective attraction favoring chiral f-wave pairing. Superconductivity is confined to a narrow metallic region adjacent to the crystal, qualitatively consistent with the superconducting sleeve observed near an insulating regime in rhombohedral graphene. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.

arxiv.title: Chemical Substitution as a Route to Anomalous Surface Superconductivity in NiBi₃
arxiv.abstract: Stabilizing two-dimensional superconductivity in a bulk superconducting material provides a unique route to exploring the interplay between superconducting condensates of different dimensionalities. Here, we present evidence for a distinct surface-associated superconducting state in Pb-substituted NiBi₃. NiBi₂.₈Pb₀.₂ exhibits a resistive onset at Tc,onset*≈8.1~K, nearly twice the bulk superconducting transition temperature of approximately 4.1~K. The absence of a corresponding Meissner response or specific-heat anomaly at the higher-temperature transition supports its non-bulk origin. A cusp-like angular dependence of the critical field, well described by the two-dimensional Tinkham model, together with nonlinear current–voltage characteristics and signatures of a Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition, establishes the low-dimensional character of this superconducting state. Remarkably, the surface-associated superconductivity persists well beyond the bulk upper critical field, reaching a maximum ratio of Hc₃/Hc₂≈4.3, far exceeding the conventional Saint-James–de Gennes value of 1.695. These results demonstrate that Pb substitution can stabilize an anomalously enhanced low-dimensional superconducting state in NiBi₃, providing a platform for investigating superconductivity at the boundary of a bulk superconductor.

arxiv.title: Finite-Temperature Transconductance of Multiterminal Josephson Junctions with Topological Andreev Spectra
arxiv.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.

arxiv.title: Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram
arxiv.abstract: We derive a mechanically consistent Ginzburg-Landau theory for the metastable heterogeneous G state reported in deeply undercooled metallic liquids. The central result is that type-II-like mixed-state physics can emerge structurally with the random internal stress field playing the role of the magnetic field. Frozen eigenstrain due to elastic incompatibility between ordered cores and the amorphous matrix generates incompatible stress, while the non-affine internal strain in the liquid-like matrix in between the ordered cores relaxes that stress over a finite screening length λσ (analogous to the London length in the superconducting problem). Structural order heals over a distinct mechanically-dressed length ξG; their ratio κG=λσ/ξG provides the structural counterpart of the Ginzburg-Landau parameter. Because the matrix is transiently rigid yet locally relaxational only over an intermediate time window, the same mechanism selects crystal for slow protocols, a heterogeneous G state at intermediate rates, and a homogeneous L-like glass under rapid arrest. Residual incompatibility frustrates coarsening, allowing finite ordered cores and screened, orientation-dependent core interactions. The resulting texture is an inverted Abrikosov analogue: structural order resides in the cores, whereas incompatible-stress screening is carried by the surrounding disordered matrix. The theory yiel

arxiv.title: Majorana Edge-to-bound State Transition in Interferometric Superconductor Rings
arxiv.abstract: Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS₂ topological superconductor. Near its superconducting transition where the coherence length exceeds the annulus width, Little-Parks oscillations exhibit expected periods for flux bundles in ring-center, consistent with edge states residing at inner and outer rims of the annulus. Upon cooling, where the coherence length shrinks below the annulus width, the unexpectedly increased oscillation period reflects multiple fluxes distributed along annulus region in flux necklace configuration, implying a transition from extended edge states to localized vortex bound states. Ginzburg-Landau simulations and local density-of-states calculations with Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations reveal that large values for both Ginzburg-Landau parameter and flux-pinning energy are vital for such a transition. Our findings provide a novel strategy for understanding flux manipulation towards flux braiding

arxiv.title: Effect of oxygen plasma treatment on the structural and superconducting properties of atomic-layer-deposited NbN thin films
arxiv.abstract: Surface oxidation is a common concern for ultrathin NbN superconducting devices, yet which superconducting properties it affects has not been established for films grown by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. We expose NbN films about 11.4 nm thick to an O₂ plasma for 0 to 60 s, which oxidizes the surface without etching the film, and characterize the same sample series by X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and transport measurements on 500 nm wide nanowires. XPS of the surface and the underlying layer shows that the plasma converts the surface to Nb₂O₅, whereas the bulk of the treated film is chemically identical to that of the untreated film. Crystalline δ-NbN remains intact. During exposure, the total film thickness rises and saturates between 40 and 60 s, indicating self-limiting surface oxide growth. The normal-state resistivity rises by 21% (dc) and 25% (optical) with the plasma dose, while the critical temperature and transition width are unchanged. The switching current densities of 4.9-6.2 MA/cm² at 4.2 K show no systematic dependence on the plasma dose. Their temperature dependence follows the dirty-limit depairing current of Kupriyanov and Lukichev, and the extrapolated switching currents reach 39-46% of the depairing current calculated from the optical resistivity and diffusion coefficient, in agreement with the width dependence reported

arxiv.title: Interplay of Chemical Disorder, Vortex Pinning, and Electron Correlations in the Mechanically Robust Medium-Entropy Alloy Superconductor Nb₀.₄₅Ta₀.₂₅Ti₀.₁₅Hf₀.₁₅
arxiv.abstract: Medium and high-entropy alloys have emerged as a promising class of superconducting materials because their intrinsic chemical disorder can simultaneously enhance mechanical robustness and modify superconducting properties. Here, we present a combined experimental and first-principles investigation of the structural, superconducting, electronic, and local lattice-distortion characteristics of the mechanically robust medium-entropy alloy Nb₀.₄₅Ta₀.₂₅Ti₀.₁₅Hf₀.₁₅. The material shows type-II superconductivity with a transition temperature TCoⁿset ≈7.8 K. A high critical current density of Jc = 0.48 ×10⁶ A/cm² is observed, and this is attributed to strong vortex pinning at grain boundaries. Specific-heat analysis indicates a strong electron-phonon coupling (λ = 1.07) with a large isotropic s-wave superconducting gap. Density functional theory calculations explicitly model the intrinsic chemical disorder, predict a stable body-centered cubic phase. These calculations further reveal a metallic electronic structure with substantial Ti- and Ta-derived states at the Fermi level. Additionally, our results quantify a pronounced disorder-induced local lattice distortion (Δd = 0.086 A), providing a microscopic basis for the experimentally observed enhanced vortex-pinning landscape. Remarkably, the alloy also exhibits an unusually large Kadowaki-Woods ratio, placing it close to the heavy-fer

arxiv.title: Strain-tunable van Hove singularity and superconducting dome in monolayer kagome metal CsTi₃Bi₅
arxiv.abstract: The recently discovered titanium-based kagome metal CsTi₃Bi₅, which exhibits superconductivity without an accompanying charge density wave, provides an ideal platform to investigate the intrinsic electronic structure and superconductivity. Moreover, it enables the exploration of superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit of the kagome lattice. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of biaxial mechanical strain (ε) on the electronic structure and superconductivity of monolayer CsTi₃Bi₅ using first-principles calculations. We demonstrate that the prominent van Hove singularity (VHS) at the M point can be monotonically tuned to the Fermi level by tensile strain. Furthermore, the superconducting transition temperature TC exhibits a dome-shaped dependence on strain, reaching a maximum of 3.6 K at an optimal tensile strain of ε=+2%. The average superconducting gap magnitude is 0.35 meV, with an orbital-dependent and anisotropic distribution. Our results provide a detailed understanding of the superconductivity of monolayer CsTi₃Bi₅ and show that strain is an effective, continuous tuning knob for manipulating the electronic structure and superconductivity.

arxiv.title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
arxiv.abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range

arxiv.title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
arxiv.abstract: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree–Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree–Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like 1s²2s² sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor D₀=√1+δ². Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source–return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

arxiv.title: Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
arxiv.abstract: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca₂CuO₂Cl₂, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates. Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". Using the MPS-based Lanczos method, we show that these localized holes give rise to in-gap bound states within the charge-transfer gap. When tunneling matrix-element effects are included, the bound states exhibit a characteristic 4a₀ ×2a₀ internal structure, consistent with experimental observations. Our results suggest that Coulomb interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets, together with tunneling matrix-element effects, provide a microscopic mechanism for the observed 4a₀ electronic structures.

arxiv.title: Cluster property and entanglement in the superconducting state
arxiv.abstract: We present the conditions for satisfying the cluster property in the superconducting state. Using these conditions, we show that the cluster property employed when deriving the order parameter of the superconducting state (OPSS) holds true, and that the OPSS is given by S⟨Ψ| hatψ(x)hatψ(x') | Ψ⟩S, where |Ψ⟩S is the superconducting state, and where hatψ(x) is the field operator of superconducting electrons. This provides a resolution to the long-standing concern raised by Leggett et al.\ regarding particle-number fluctuation in the superconducting state. In addition, by considering the entanglement between two particles composed of the maximum geminal of the BCS ground state [J.\ Phys. Commun. 5, 095003 (2021)], it is confirmed that the larger the deviation from the conditions for satisfying the cluster property becomes, the greater the magnitude of the entanglement becomes. This shows not only the effectiveness of the conditions for satisfying the cluster property but also the justification of the OPSS that has been commonly used.

arxiv.title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
arxiv.abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50–60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35–40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.

arxiv.title: Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
arxiv.abstract: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase. Here we investigate the in-plane thermoelectric response of this eutectic system in the normal state and find a pronounced anisotropy in the thermopower for thermal gradients applied parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae. To clarify its origin, we combine thermopower measurements with electronic-structure-based transport calculations and finite-element modeling of the local strain distribution generated by the thermal-expansion mismatch between Sr2RuO4 and Ru. The calculations show that uniaxial compression of Sr2RuO4 produces a sizable thermopower anisotropy through modification of the Fermi surfaces. When an idealized spatially inhomogeneous strain field around the Ru lamellae is included, the observed sign and qualitative magnitude of the anisotropy are reproduced more closely than in a simple unstrained two-component model. These results are consistent with a substantial contribution from strain-induced changes in the Sr2RuO4 electronic structure near the interfaces, although contributions from interfacial phase mixing and three-dimensional transport connectivity cannot be excluded.

arxiv.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
arxiv.abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform d-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At 1/8 doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform d-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-t energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

arxiv.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
arxiv.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates–-close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns–-with intrinsic errors suppressed to the 2×10⁻⁵ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from 1/f flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

arxiv.title: NTL amplification in a SuperCDMS-style detector fabricated from a University of South Dakota-grown germanium crystal
arxiv.abstract: Neganov-Trofimov-Luke (NTL) amplification enables eV-sub-keV detection thresholds for low-mass dark-matter and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments. We evaluated two University of South Dakota (USD)-grown germanium crystals fabricated as SuperCDMS-style four-channel athermal-phonon detectors and operated near 10 mK. The crystals had electrically active impurity concentrations near 10¹0 mathrm⁻3 and etch-pit densities of 300-7000 mathrm⁻2. Contact-free biasing produced no resolvable amplification. However, after depositing a 600 nm aluminum bias contact, Detector~2 exhibited clear voltage-dependent NTL gain. The reconstructed channel-B energy increased from approximately 3.9 keV at 0 V to 34.9 keV at 40 V, corresponding to an 8.9-fold enhancement. Statistical centroid uncertainties were below 0.3%, while low-bias fits yielded effective prompt- and NTL-phonon response coefficients of (6.77±0.82)% and (4.77±0.20)%, respectively, excluding systematic uncertainties. These results demonstrate the feasibility of USD-grown germanium for SuperCDMS-style high-voltage phonon detectors and highlight the importance of both crystal quality and contact fabrication in achieving NTL amplification.

arxiv.title: Unambiguous determination of the THz conductivity in driven YBa₂Cu₃O₆₊ₓ
arxiv.abstract: Mid-infrared pump, THz probe experiments in YBa₂Cu₃O₆₊ₓ yield evidence of a high-temperature transient state of the material with the optical properties of a superconductor. However, there are ambiguities in the extracted transient c-axis THz optical properties, primarily resulting from the sublinear growth of the THz response with increasing mid-infrared pump fluence. It was proposed that this effect may be related to saturation of the material's response, which would then perturb its spatial profile and lead one to overestimate the induced change in the transient optical properties. Yet, sublinear growth of the signal could also arise from other effects unrelated to saturation, for example from a change in reflectivity or deposition depth for the pump pulses. Here, we remove this ambiguity by experimentally measuring the fluence-dependent complex optical constants at the 15-20 THz frequencies of the pump. We show that the observed sublinear growth is to be attributed in large part to the enhanced reflection and reduced penetration depth of the pump field at high fluences. When taking into account these findings, we confirm the original interpretation of a light-induced superconducting state both qualitatively and quantitatively.

arxiv.title: Geometrization of continuum mechanics and nonequilibrium thermodynamics: Heat conduction
arxiv.abstract: We propose a geometric formulation of non-equilibrium heat conduction. It combines the variational (Hamiltonian) structure of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) equations with the exterior calculus of differential forms. The central object is the thermal impulse one-form on the four-dimensional matter-time manifold. Its time component is the temperature, and for reversible (ballistic) heat transport it is the exact differential of a scalar potential (i.e. it is holonomic). Non-equilibrium effects are described by a second one-form, the small-scale thermal impulse, which is not required to be exact. Its time component is a fluctuating temperature, and its exterior derivative, the four-thermal vorticity, satisfies a Bianchi-type kinematic identity. The variational principle together with this identity yields a non-equilibrium two-temperature model. Its field equations have the same structure as Maxwell's equations in a medium, with the thermal impulse field, the thermal vorticity field and a thermal Poynting vector contributing to the heat flux. Dissipation is introduced through relaxation terms that conserve the total energy and produce entropy. A formal asymptotic analysis shows that, in the relaxation limit, the model reduces to a Guyer-Krumhansl-type heat conduction with independent transverse and longitudinal length scales. The transverse nonlocal term

arxiv.title: Superconductivity via repulsive interaction in the model with electrons and holes
arxiv.abstract: We study a toy model of the 2D electron gas including electron-like and hole-like charge carriers hybridized between each other. Electrons and holes can move either in different layers or in the same layer. Undoped system is an insulator. Slight doping brings extra charge carriers having large density of states. We show that the screened Coulomb interaction is enough to stabilize the superconductivity in the slightly doped system. The symmetry of the order parameter corresponds to the spin-triplet p-wave order. For realistic values of the model parameters the superconducting transition temperature can reach the value of 150 kelvin.

arxiv.title: Suppressing Majorana Hybridization in Atomically Assembled Cr Chains on Bi2Pd
arxiv.abstract: Magnetic-atom chains on superconductors can host Majorana zero modes, but in finite chains the two end modes generally hibridize and split away from zero energy. We show that Cr chains assembled atom-by-atom on the Bi-terminated surface of Bi2Pd enter a short-localization-length Shiba chain regime wthat strongly suppreesses this finite-size hybridization. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a chaing-leght-driven closing and reopening of the in-gap spectrum, followed by zero-bias modes localized at the chains ends. Green-function calculations reproduce the evolution and show an exchange of electorn-holec haracter across the transition. From the residual splitting we extract a localization length of about three atomic sites, explaining the stability of the zero-energy modes in experimentally accessible chains.

arxiv.title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr₆Sb₆
arxiv.abstract: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr₆Sb₆, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below TF∼70 K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of ∼30-80 K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature Tp∼20-25 K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr₆Sb₆ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

arxiv.title: Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
arxiv.abstract: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging. We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents. Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR. Numerical simulations combining magnetization dynamics and Josephson phase dynamics reproduce these features, confirming that the JDE originates from interfacial coupling between magnetization and Josephson current. This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.

arxiv.title: Exotic vortex states and enhancement of orbital upper critical fields in an s-wave quasicrystalline superconductor
arxiv.abstract: Quasicrystals possess long-range order without translational symmetry, giving rise to intrinsically inhomogeneous superconducting states. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes mean-field theory, we investigate vortex states in an s-wave quasicrystalline superconductor on the Ammann-Beenker tiling, with particular emphasis on the high-field regime. We find that the vortex configuration can differ qualitatively from the Abrikosov triangular lattice. In particular, at filling ν=0.8, vortices preferentially penetrate weak-pairing regions centered on sites with coordination number 8, indicating that their spatial organization is strongly influenced by the local geometry. Furthermore, we observe an enhanced upper critical field. At ν=0.8, where the enhancement is particularly pronounced, the spatially averaged order parameter exhibits a plateau-like field dependence accompanied by the formation of vortex clusters. These clusters accommodate additional flux in locally weak superconducting regions, providing a microscopic interpretation of the plateau-like behavior. Moreover, the upper critical field increases upon cooling toward zero temperature without a clear sign of saturation.

arxiv.title: Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
arxiv.abstract: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance R_n, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.

arxiv.title: Theory of the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall responses in time-reversal symmetry breaking superconductors
arxiv.abstract: Determining the symmetry of the Cooper pairing in superconductors is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. Time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) is among the most distinctive symmetry-breaking pattern of a superconductor. An important subset of TRSB pairing states, including the topological pₓ+ipy pairing, is expected to exhibit the optical anomalous Hall effect. However, the microscopic ingredients that enable the Hall response and their underlying organizing principle in clean superconductors remain unelucidated. Here, we develop a unified theory for TRSB multiband superconductors possessing inversion symmetry, and establish their intrinsic optical Hall response as fundamentally a quantum-geometric phenomenon. We distinguish unitary and nonunitary TRSB states. Diagrammatically, we identify two classes of processes: single-electron tunneling and Cooper-pair tunneling. Both involve at least one interband tunneling event driven by the interband velocity-which is closely tied to the interband Berry connection. We rigorously prove that interband pairing is a prerequisite for unitary states to generate intrinsic Hall response, whereas it is not absolutely needed for nonunitary states. In nonunitary states with intraband pairing alone, the Hall effect can arise through single-electron tunneling, provided spin-orbit coupling is present. An effective theory obtained by int

arxiv.title: Saturating T² resistivity in iron-based superconductors
arxiv.abstract: Many correlated metals exhibit a crossover from low-temperature ρ∝T² behavior to a slower increase of the resistivity at elevated temperatures. Distinguishing phonon scattering from electron–electron correlations as the origin of this crossover is experimentally challenging. We introduce a simple phenomenological framework that isolates the contribution responsible for the high-temperature saturating tendency. This approach reveals a clear contrast between systems well known for the predominance of electron–phonon scattering and several iron-based superconductors. For the latter, the conductivity can be expressed as the sum of a Fermi-liquid-like term (∝1/T²) and a temperature-independent component, which together describe ρ(T) up to ∼250 K in LiFeAs, KFe₂As₂, and KCaFe₄As₄. In FeSe, the same approach identifies a similar regime above the nematic transition, with a pronounced change toward nearly linear-in-T resistivity below it. We discuss these findings in the broader context of coherence and electronic correlations in Hund's metals.

arxiv.title: Superconducting weak links at substrate steps in bilayer nickelate films
arxiv.abstract: Ambient-pressure superconductivity above 40 K has been realized in bilayer nickelate thin films on SrLaAlO₄ (001), yet resistive measurements often exhibit incomplete zero-resistance states and/or two-step superconducting transitions of unresolved origin. We show that these features arise from superconducting weak links at substrate step-terrace structures. A direct correlation between the azimuthal-angle-dependent two-step transition and step-terrace orientation establishes this connection, further supported by atomic-scale visualization of structurally disrupted regions at step terraces. Modeling the films as pristine (weak-link) regions with higher (lower) transition temperature reproduces essential features of the two-step transition using both a simple model and finite-element simulations. Transport measurements further reveal a strong dependence of transition characteristics - and even the occurrence of superconductivity itself - on average terrace width. These results identify step-induced weak links as the microscopic origin of two-step transitions in bilayer nickelate films, providing a framework for understanding anisotropic and percolative transport, and a route to superconducting devices.

arxiv.title: Non-uniform grids to accelerate electron-phonon coupling calculations for superconductivity
arxiv.abstract: Efficient and accurate evaluation of electron-phonon interactions is essential for predictive superconductivity calculations, but dense Brillouin zone sampling requirements pose a major computational bottleneck. To overcome this, we introduce an accelerated, highly scalable framework that combines a double delta truncation scheme with non-uniform Farey grids in both k and q space. The truncation strategy significantly reduces computational cost by restricting integration to states satisfying energy constraints near the Fermi level, while the Farey grids dynamically resolve sampling errors from localized scattering and stabilize convergence. Applied to elemental aluminium and several high-pressure hydrides, this combined methodology reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude and yields electron-phonon coupling constants and superconducting critical temperatures Tc typically within about 5% of full-grid benchmarks. This approach overcomes sampling bottlenecks associated with dense uniform grids, making accurate, low-cost predictions of superconductivity in complex quantum materials feasible.

arxiv.title: Andreev Scattering Driven Surface Photogalvanic Effect
arxiv.abstract: The surface photogalvanic effect is a powerful tool for generating macroscopic direct currents in centrosymmetric film structures via asymmetric scattering of carriers at film boundaries. Here, we uncover a fundamentally distinct regime of photoinduced transport in normal metal-superconductor heterostructures, in which the macroscopic photocurrent is governed by Andreev scattering at the interface rather than by classical scattering. We demonstrate that the interplay between asymmetric surface scattering and Andreev retroreflection yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent anomalous photocurrent. Strikingly, the electron-hole conversion at the normal-superconducting interface dictates a macroscopic sign reversal of the photogalvanic current across the superconducting transition, and induces non-analytic spectral kinks exactly at the pairing gap frequency. Our results establish the Andreev reflection-driven surface photogalvanic effect as a platform for optical control of superconducting correlations and suggest a direct, non-invasive spectroscopic probe for gap dynamics in hybrid quantum devices.

arxiv.title: Pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal
arxiv.abstract: We propose a model that explains the mechanism of pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal. Four types of pair potentials are assumed for a Cooper pair consisting of two electrons on different layers. Absence of local inversion symmetry gives rise to the spin-orbit coupling which is antisymmetric in the two layers. We assume that external pressure enhances the hybridization between the two layers. The stability of the superconducting states is well explained by the frequency symmetry of the induced pairing correlations by these potentials. Pressure-induced superconductivity emerges when the following two conditions are realized. (i) The spin-orbit coupling induces the odd-frequency pairing correlations and suppresses superconductivity at ambient pressure. (ii) The interplay between the spin-orbit coupling and the hybridization induces the additional pairing correlation that belongs to an even-frequency symmetry class. We briefly discuss the relevance of our model to real materials.

Symmetry-indicator theory and topological quantum chemistry provide an efficient scheme to diagnose topological phases from only partial information of wave functions without full knowledge of topological invariants, which has resulted in a recent comprehensive materials search. However, not all topological phases can be captured by this framework, and topological invariants are needed for a more refined diagnosis of topological phases. In this study, we present a systematic framework to construct topological invariants for a large part of symmetry classes, which should be contrasted with the existing invariants discovered through one-by-one approaches. Our method is based on the recently developed Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space. As a demonstration, we construct topological invariants for time-reversal-symmetric spinful superconductors with conventional pairing symmetries of all space groups, for which symmetry indicators are silent. We also validate that the obtained quantities work as topological invariants by computing them for randomly generated symmetric Hamiltonians. Remarkably, the constructed topological invariants completely characterize K groups in 159 space groups. Our topological invariants for normal conducting phases are defined under some gauge condit

Nontrivial Boundary-Mediated Superconducting Transport in a TRSB Topological Iron-Based Superconductor
journals.abstract: The interplay of superconductivity, band topology, and spontaneous time-reversal-symmetry breaking (TRSB) is expected to enable topological superconducting boundary states. Intriguingly, the iron-chalcogenide superconductor FeTe 0.55 Se 0.45 exhibits spontaneous magnetization in the superconducting state, motivating its use as a single-material platform in which three ingredients coexist. Here, we report evidence for a nontrivial, boundary-mediated superconducting transport response in exfoliated Fe(Te,Se) devices, exhibiting long-range nonlocality and strongly suppressed thermal broadening. Polar Kerr measurements establish that TRSB emerges below T Kerr < T c and coexists with superconductivity across multiple Fe(Te,Se) compositions studied here, providing an independent symmetry-breaking scale that can be directly compared with transport. To reliably access boundary transport, we engineer crystallographically sharp, continuous edges and implement side-surface-dominant contacts, as validated by contact-size analysis and cross-sectional imaging. Under these conditions, topological FeTe 0.55 Se 0.45 exhibits an anomalous conductance plateau that is absent in topologically trivial FeTe 0.40 Se 0.60 and Fe 1.02 Te 0.55 Se 0.45 under comparable measurements. journals.abstract: In conventional, phonon-mediated superconductors, the transition temperature and the linear-in-temperature normal-state scattering rate are linked through the electron–phonon coupling strength. In cuprate high-temperature superconductors, no equivalent relationship between critical temperature and electron–boson coupling has been identified. Here we highlight such a link with electrons scattering off commensurate antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations of variable strength. We use d.c. resistivity and high-field magnetoresistance to extract the scattering rate in electron-doped La ₂− ₓ Ce ₓ CuO ₄ as a function of doping. We reveal a highly anisotropic inelastic component to the scattering rate whose magnitude diminishes markedly as doping increases. The correlation we highlight between the strength of scattering and the critical temperature then identifies low-energy spin fluctuations as the primary pairing glue in electron-doped cuprates. The contrasting magnetotransport behaviour in hole-doped cuprates suggests that the higher critical temperature in those materials cannot be attributed solely to an increase in the coupling strength to the antiferromagnetic fluctuations. journals.abstract: Side surfaces of cuprate superconductors are expected to display a suppressed d -wave order parameter and zero-energy topological flat bands with a large density of states, making them susceptible to symmetry broken orders. Yet such surfaces have never been investigated with momentum-resolved, surface-sensitive probes, because high-temperature superconductors rarely cleave along them. Using focused-ion-beam milling to define a controlled breaking point, we expose pristine (110) side surfaces of overdoped La ₂− ₓ Sr ₓ CuO ₄ ( x = 0.22) suitable for angle-resolved photoemission. We do not resolve an opening or closing of a superconducting spectral gap within our energy resolution ( ~ 4 meV), in agreement with theoretical predictions. Surprisingly, the expected zero-energy flat band peak is also suppressed, despite the high topographic quality of the surface. Self-consistent Bogoliubov–de Gennes calculations show that the measured geometric roughness of the cleaved surface is too weak to eliminate these modes. The calculations further demonstrate that bulk inhomogeneities characteristic of high-temperature superconductors, modelled as moderate Anderson-type disorder, can broaden the flat-band states beyond detectability. journals.title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness and Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity in UTe 2
journals.abstract: Superconductivity in three dimensions is almost universally governed by Ginzburg-Landau mean-field theory, with critical fluctuations typically confined to within a few percent of the transition temperature ( T c ). We report that the heavy-fermion superconductor UTe 2 exhibits superconducting fluctuations that extend over a temperature range as wide as T c itself—the largest observed for any three-dimensional superconductor. Through ultrasound measurements of the elastic moduli and sound attenuation, we find that UTe 2 transitions from a mean-field-like state at ambient pressure to a fluctuation-dominated state at higher pressures. This regime is marked by elastic softening and an increase in sound attenuation that onsets well above T c , with the attenuation remaining anomalously high deep in the superconducting state. Our analysis suggests that these features stem from an extremely low superfluid phase stiffness. This results in a kinetic inductance as high as that of granular aluminum, but achieved in the clean limit. We propose a model where this exotic state is driven by dominant interband pairing mediated by ferromagnetic fluctuations, leading to “local” Cooper pairs with a coherence length of only a few lattice constants.

journals.abstract: Accessing the intrinsic critical current density in type-II superconductors can provide a means to probe microscopic superconducting properties and increase current limits in high-magnetic-field devices and electrical power systems. However, the critical current density measured using direct currents generally lies below this intrinsic limit, mainly because of vortex motion and self-heating. Here we show that picosecond electrical pulses, which act on timescales too short for vortices to move, drive supercurrents up to the intrinsic depairing limit. We probe picosecond critical currents in NbN and YBa ₂ Cu ₃ O ₇ , representative s -wave and d -wave superconductors, respectively. In NbN, we find a sharp onset of the picosecond depairing at a current density of about 2.2 times the conventional critical current density, consistent with microscopic dynamics based on Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer theory. By contrast, YBa ₂ Cu ₃ O ₇ exhibits a gradual suppression of superconductivity with increasing current, reflecting its d -wave symmetry. These results provide a probe of superconductors beyond the reach of conventional transport measurements. Attaining the depairing current could also support superconducting electronics operating closer to intrinsic current limits.

journals.abstract: Cuprate superconductors remain central to condensed matter physics due to their technological relevance and unconventional, incompletely understood electronic behavior. While the canonical phase diagram and low-energy models have been shaped largely by studies of underdoped and moderately doped cuprates, the overdoped regime has received comparatively limited attention. Here, we track the evolution of the electronic structure from optimal to heavy overdoping in La ₂−ₓ Sr ₓ CuO ₄ (LSCO) using broadband optical spectroscopy across x = 0.15–0.60. The measured spectral changes—including the redistribution of Zhang–Rice–related spectral weight—are in qualitative agreement with determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations of the three-orbital Emery model, which together indicate a pronounced reconstruction of the electronic structure beyond hole concentrations x > 0.2. Guided by these observations, we propose a spontaneous checkerboard-type Zhang–Rice electronic configuration that accounts for the coexistence of itinerant and localized carriers characteristic of the heavily overdoped state. journals.abstract: Structural phase transitions generate complex microstructures that often govern material functionality, yet directly resolving their three-dimensional organization in bulk samples remains challenging. Here we employ scanning three-dimensional x-ray diffraction (3DXRD) to resolve the bulk microstructure of La 1.675 Eu 0.2 Sr 0.125 CuO 4 , a prototypical 1 / 8 -doped cuprate in which structural and electronic heterogeneity is well established. We reveal remarkably broad tetragonallike domain wall regions within the nominally orthorhombic crystal structure, and, upon cooling to 100 K, a fine microstructure of orthorhombiclike stripes embedded within the tetragonal matrix that has significant consequences for interpreting the interplay between structural and electronic heterogeneity in this class of materials. More broadly, this work establishes 3DXRD as a powerful approach for resolving bulk microstructures and understanding their role in emergent functionality.

journals.title: Superconductivity in Monolayer-Trilayer Phase of La 3 Ni 2 O 7 under High Pressure
journals.abstract: The discovery of 80 K superconductivity in pressurized bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7 has established a new high-temperature superconductor family [1]. The quest to understand the governing principles of RP nickelate superconductivity has become a central focus in condensed matter physics. Here, we report a critical advance by synthesizing and investigating a distinct structural polymorph of the same compound: the monolayer-trilayer (1313) phase of La 3 Ni 2 O 7 . Under high pressure, synchrotron x-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy reveal a structural transition from the orthorhombic C m m m to the tetragonal P 4 / m m m space group at 13 GPa. Above 19 GPa, the phase shows a clear superconducting transition, confirmed by a zero-resistance state, albeit at a much lower temperature of 3.6 K. The stark contrast with the 80 K transition in the bilayer phase provides a uniquely clean experimental comparison. Our results not only expand the family of RP nickelate superconductors but also deepen the understanding of the superconducting mechanism that governs the transition temperature in these materials.

journals.abstract: Multiphase superconductors—materials that host two or more distinct superconductive phases—are exceptionally rare. Examples include heavy-fermion CeRh ₂ As ₂ alongside some uranium compounds such as UPt ₃ and URhGe (refs. ¹,²,³ ). In the multiphase p -wave superfluid ³ He, complex vortex dynamics can occur at the phase boundary between the A and B phases ⁴,⁵ . Here we study the p -wave superconductor candidate UTe ₂ (refs. ⁶–⁸ ). On applying a magnetic field to access an intermediate regime straddling two distinct superconducting phases ⁹,¹⁰ , we find that direct current pulses can push the material in and out of a metastable state that has an enhanced critical current density J c . This switching is controllable by the strength and duration of the stimuli, with the system ‘remembering’ whether it is in the high or low J c state for extended periods. We interpret this phenomenology to be due to the quenching of a disordered out-of-equilibrium glassy vortex state under perturbation, which has stronger pinning forces and thus higher J c . The equilibrium vortex lattice is reattained by annealing the system with a gradual current ramp, returning it to the original state. Rather than requiring proximate magnetic or semiconducting interfaces ¹¹–¹⁴ , this memory functionality seems to be an intrinsic property of UTe ₂ rooted in the superconducting order itself. journals.title: Effective Ionic Valence and Local Magnetic Moment in Kagome Superconductors
journals.abstract: In order to understand the unexpected similarity and the correlated behavior in kagome superconductor families A V 3 Sb 5 ( A = K , Rb , Cs ) and A Ti 3 Bi 5 ( A = Rb , Cs ), we investigate the Hartree-scale local electronic structure of these systems. Our result indicates that V and Ti ions are both of 2 + valence such that the corresponding itinerant carrier densities are similar, and the difference in electron count is instead reflected in their quantum fluctuating ionic magnetic moments. However, due to the frustrated lattice geometry of these materials, such local moments are difficult to experimentally observe via standard probes. For verification, we systematically introduce nonmagnetic Sn impurities to locally relieve the geometric frustration and experimentally demonstrate the existence of well-defined local magnetic moments via magnetic susceptibility and muon spin rotation or relaxation ( μ SR ) measurements. All experiments discover a systematic increase of magnetic susceptibility upon increasing nonmagnetic impurity level. Our discovered ionic moments suggest a paradigm shift from the existing itinerant carrier-only picture to one incorporating strong correlation from local ionic spins. journals.title: Berry curvature multipoles in Kagome superconductor CsV3Sb5
journals.abstract: Electronic nematic transitions in correlated systems often involve substantial reorganization of Berry curvature. Nonlinear transport measurements serve as a powerful tool for distinguishing between different types of Berry curvature multipoles that characterize nematic phases and topological changes. Herein, we systematically measured nonlinear responses up to the sixth harmonic in the Kagome superconductor CsV ₃ Sb ₅ . Our results identify the odd-order nonlinear Hall effect as the dominant signature of nematicity. During the superconducting transition, vortex dynamics induce rapid spatial variations in the phase gradient ∇ ϕ, which significantly amplify the Berry curvature quadrupole (BCQ) relative to Berry curvature dipole (BCD). The third-order nonlinear response peaks sharply near the superconducting transition, where enhanced vortex–antivortex fluctuations and nonlinear vortex dynamics amplify the BCQ-related nonlinear Hall response. First-principles calculations further support this interpretation by revealing pronounced Berry-curvature quadrupoles induced by chiral loop-current order near the Fermi level. This work establishes BCQ as a sensitive probe of electronic nematicity, particularly when enhanced by superconducting vortex dynamics.

Flux-Floquet Instability in Fluctuating Superconductors
journals.abstract: In the past decade, photoinduced superconductinglike behaviors have been reported in a number of materials driven by intense pump fields. Of particular interest is the high- T c cuprate YBa 2 C u 3 O 6 + x (YBCO), where such effect has been reported up to the so-called pseudogap temperature T * ∼ 300 – 400 K . In a recent tour-de-force experiment, a transient magnetic field which is proportional to and in the same direction of an applied field has been observed outside the sample, suggestive of flux exclusion due to the Meissner effect. In this paper, we present an alternative interpretation of these experiments based on a mechanism that we term the flux-Floquet instability of the sine-Gordon (SG) model. We take as our premise the model of preformed Cooper pairs in the pseudogap phase. Starting from the local superconducting order parameter in equilibrium, we introduce an extended SG model to describe the dynamics of the relative phase between the layers of a bilayer. We demonstrate that a combination of external magnetic field and strong terahertz drive used in experiments by Fava results in a novel Floquet instability in the model. journals.abstract: Quantum routers (QRouters) are essential components of bucket-brigade quantum random access memory (QRAM), enabling quantum applications such as Grover’s search and quantum machine learning. Despite significant theoretical advances, achieving scalable and coherent QRouters experimentally remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate coherent quantum routers using a superconducting quantum processor, laying a practical foundation for scalable QRAM systems. The quantum router at the core of our implementation utilizes the transition composite gate scheme, wherein auxiliary energy levels temporarily mediate conditional interactions. By leveraging two-qubit primitives in its construction, the quantum router preserves straightforward initialization and calibration while significantly reducing circuit depth and duration relative to traditional gate-based decompositions. Moreover, by encoding routing addresses in the nonadjacent qutrit states | 0 ⟩ and | 2 ⟩ , our design inherently enables erasure-detection capability, providing efficient postselection to mitigate routing errors. Experimentally, we achieve an average fidelity of 94.8% across three individual QRouters, and we validate scalability through a two-layer quantum routing network achieving a fidelity of 82.4%. journals.abstract: The origin of superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene has been a subject of intense debate. While some experimental evidence indicated an unconventional pairing mechanism which should be sensitive to Coulomb screening, experimental attempts to tune the critical temperature by screening Coulomb interactions so far have remained unsuccessful, possibly indicating a conventional phonon-mediated pairing. Here we study a double-layer electronic system consisting of two twisted graphene bilayers in immediate proximity of each other but remaining electronically decoupled. By increasing the carrier density in one bilayer, we completely suppressed both the superconductivity and the correlated-insulator state in the adjacent magic-angle graphene. The observation of such an effect from screening offers support for an unconventional mechanism of Cooper pairing in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, shedding new light on the underlying physics governing their properties.

journals.abstract: We investigate the bilayer nickelates as a platform to realize the symmetric mass generation (SMG) insulator, a featureless Mott insulator that arises due to the Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) anomaly cancellation in bilayer spin-1/2 lattice systems. Through a single-orbital bilayer square lattice model involving intralayer hopping t and interlayer superexchange interaction J , we demonstrate the emergence of high-temperature superconductivity (SC) upon doping the SMG insulator. The SC phase features s -wave interlayer spin-singlet pairing and exhibits a crossover between the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) and Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) limits by tuning the J / t ratio. We estimate the SC transition temperature T c from both the weak and strong coupling limits at the mean-field level. Our findings offer insights into the experimentally observed decrease in T c with pressure and the strange metal behavior above T c . Additionally, we propose that both Ni 3dz² 3 d z 2 and 3dx²-y² 3 d x 2 − y 2 orbitals can exhibit superconductivity in La ₃ Ni ₂ O ₇ under pressure, but their T c should vary in opposite ways under doping. This characteristic difference suggests a potential experimental pathway to identify which electronic orbital plays the principal role in the formation of superconductivity in this system.

journals.title: Orientational enhancement of surface phonon polarity in superconducting KTaO₃ interfaces
journals.abstract: The critical role of symmetry-breaking interfaces in mediating superconductivity has garnered increasing interest in recent years. KTaO ₃ (KTO)-based heterointerfaces present a striking example, where the superconducting transition temperature ( T c ) exhibits an intriguing dependence on KTO crystallographic orientation. Here we identify a highly anisotropic surface phonon resonance near 107 meV at KTO and KTO-based heterointerfaces using surface-specific, symmetry-sensitive nonlinear optical spectroscopy. Polarity of this phonon mode scales with crystallographic orientation as (111) > (110) ≫ (001), reaching a 35-fold enhancement over non-superconducting interfaces and tracking the superconducting T c . In addition, a softened local mode near 100 meV is observed and attributed to interfacial oxygen vacancies. Our results help build a framework linking the symmetry-breaking lattice phonons, defects, and anisotropic superconductivity for KTO and related heterointerfaces.

Superconducting materials exhibiting high uniformity, large absorption cross-section and atomic-scale thickness are desirable to extend single-photon detection from the near-infrared up to the terahertz regime, where existing material choices are especially constrained. Substrate independence would further open the way to integrating detectors onto functional materials and heterostructures, enhancing performance and enabling proximal readout of a wide range of individual excitations. At the same time, the dark-count rate remains below 1 Hz up to the switching current and we achieve a timing jitter below 50 ps. We estimate via a diffusive hot-spot model that materials and geometric parameters would allow a theoretical cut-off wavelength in the millimetre range, assuming state-of-the-art device parameters. journals.abstract: The kagome metals A V ₃ Sb ₅ ( A = Cs, Rb, K) host multiple symmetry-breaking phases, including charge-density-wave and loop-current orders, and exhibit highly exotic superconductivity with pronounced nematicity and chirality. Remarkably, even dilute impurities transform this exotic superconducting state into an isotropic s -wave state. These observations pose a challenge to existing theoretical scenarios. We show that loop-current order induces nematic chiral d -wave superconductivity in kagome metals. The loop-current-induced orbital magnetization (OM) stabilizes one chiral superconducting channels. This OM-chirality coupling mechanism is generic and applies to pairing driven by either attractive or repulsive interactions. Furthermore, coexisting loop-current and bond orders give rise to pronounced nematic chiral superconductivity even for an almost C ₆ -symmetric Fermi surface. For attractive pairing, dilute impurities suppress the chiral state and restore a conventional s -wave phase, as observed experimentally. The theory further predicts a robust 2 × 2 pair-density modulation. This study provides key insights into time-reversal-symmetry-breaking exotic superconductivity in kagome metals.

journals.title: Three-Dimensional Electronic Structures in Superconducting Ruddlesden-Popper Bilayer Nickelate Films
journals.abstract: Beyond the quasi-two-dimensional (2D) paradigm of cuprates, the role of the third dimension of the Ruddlesden-Popper bilayer nickelates is essential to decoding their superconducting mechanism. Here, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) with varied photon energies, we systematically investigate the electronic band structures in three dimensions for superconducting ( La , Pr , Sm ) 3 Ni 2 O 7 / SrLaAlO 4 thin films (superconducting onset temperature T c onset ∼ 48 K ) transferred via a cryogenic ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) suitcase. We reveal an orbital-dependent dimensionality: While the d x 2 − y 2 -dominant bands exhibit a quasi-2D character, the d z 2 -dominant band displays a finite k z dispersion. Finite energy gaps are identified on all observed bands across multiple high-symmetry directions. Systematic temperature-dependent analysis characterizes the superconducting nature of the gap on the d z 2 -derived band, revealing a large gap Δ ∼ 18 meV and a ratio 2 Δ / k B T c ∼ 8 exceeding the weak-coupling BCS limit. The suppression of spectral weight near the Fermi level persists above the superconducting transition temperature. Ubiquitous vertical spectral features evidence the presence of electron interactions. These results underscore the role of the d z 2 orbital and correlations, placing constraints on theoretical models for nickelate superconductivity.

journals.abstract: It was recently discovered that supercurrents flowing through thin superconducting nanowires can be quenched by applying a gate voltage to a nearby gate electrode. This gate control of supercurrents, known as the GCS effect, could enable superconducting transistor logic. Here, we report that the GCS also manifests in a suppression of Meissner screening, establishing the phenomenon as a genuine feature of superconductivity that is not restricted to transport. Using a scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometer at sub-Kelvin temperatures, we image the nanoscale spatial region of GCS suppression in micron-size niobium islands. Our observations are compatible with a microscopic hot-spot model of quasiparticle generation and diffusion, and in conflict with other candidate mechanisms such as Joule heating or an electric field effect. Our work introduces an alternative means for studying quasiparticle dynamics in superconducting nanostructures, and showcases the power of local imaging techniques for understanding emergent condensed matter phenomena.

journals.abstract: Understanding the emergence of unconventional superconductivity, where the order parameter deviates from simple isotropic s-wave pairing, is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. Some transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), though generally regarded as conventional superconductors, display signatures of unconventional pairing and thus provide a particularly intriguing platform to explore how exotic states arise. Here we investigate the misfit compound (SnS) ₁.₁₅ (TaS ₂ ), a heterostructure composed of alternating SnS and 1H-TaS ₂ layers. Using transport, photoemission, and scanning tunneling spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the SnS layers effectively decouple the TaS ₂ into electronically isolated 1H sheets. In this limit, the tunneling density of states on the 1H layer reveals a clear two-gap superconducting spectrum with T c ≃ 3.1 K. A theoretical model based on lack of inversion symmetry of the system and finite-range attraction reproduces the observed multi-gap structure as a mixed singlet-triplet state. These results establish misfit compounds as a powerful platform for studying unconventional superconductivity in isolated 1H layers and for realizing multiple uncoupled superconductors within a single crystal.

journals.abstract: In multilayered high- T c cuprates, the inner CuO ₂ planes (IPs) are spatially separated from dopant layers and thus remain cleaner than the outer planes (OPs). Here, we investigate five-layer (Cu,C)Ba ₂ Ca ₄ Cu ₅ O y (Cu1245) and three-layer Ba ₂ Ca ₂ Cu ₃ O ₆ (F,O) ₂ (F0223) using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and uncover an unprecedented situation, in which only the IPs become superconducting while the OPs remain metallic at low temperatures. Our model calculations indicate that over 95% of the OP wavefunction remains confined to OP itself, rendering superconducting proximity negligible. This interlayer decoupling realizes an ideal configuration—a single superconducting CuO ₂ layer screened from the dopant layer-induced disorder by heavily overdoped metallic OPs. The clean CuO ₂ layer exhibits a large superconducting gap with coherent Bogoliubov peaks extending beyond the antiferromagnetic zone boundary, and a widely extended coherent flat band at the Brillouin zone edge. These findings introduce the “degree of screening” as a physical parameter for probing competition between pseudogap and superconductivity, and for bridging typically disordered real materials with the idealized theoretical models.

journals.abstract: Magnetic fields can penetrate a superconductor in the form of quantum vortices, which consist of a core singularity with circulating currents. London’s quantization implies that there is one core singularity per quantum of magnetic flux in single-component superconductors. In this study, we report signatures of quantum vortex core fractionalization on the potassium-terminated surface of a multiband superconductor, KFe ₂ As ₂ . The observed splitting of single integer–flux vortices into several fractional vortices results in a disparity between the numbers of flux quanta and vortex cores. These fractional vortices often arrange in chains, which calculations show are characterized by a ℂP ² skyrmionic topological invariant; this constitutes a different type of topological defect: the chiral skyrmion. The disparate natures of integer and fractional vortices comprising skyrmions lead to distinct spectroscopic signatures.
